text:
Punishment, as an actual social institution, operates independently of any moral reasons offered for it, so the two have to be kept apart. Because the practice exists whether or not it is justified, we need a separate standard (retribution, deterrence, or rehabilitation) to judge it. Each of those standards limits who may be punished, how severely, and for how long. If the two are merged, any punishment looks justified just because it exists, and we can no longer criticize or reform it.
